key_insight: Parallel execution across multiple on-premises QPUs can speed up fragment-based quantum chemistry without sacrificing chemical accuracy.
engineering_relevance: The work shows how future HPC systems could treat several quantum processors as a distributed resource to increase throughput for molecular simulation workflows.
method: Use fragment molecular orbital (FMO) decomposition to split a molecule into smaller quantum chemistry subproblems.
Compare synchronous shot-parallel execution with asynchronous fragment-parallel execution on three room-temperature diamond-based QPUs.
Run Quantum Wave Function Sampler (QWFS) selected configuration interaction calculations on helium clusters and assemble SPAM-corrected results.
evidence_signal: On helium clusters He$_n$ (n=2, 4, 8, 10, 14), the three-QPU workflow achieved 93.60% parallel efficiency for shot-parallel execution and 75.01% for fragment-parallel execution, rising to 95.17% after excluding idle time, while maintaining chemically accurate energies.
watch_item: The reported efficiency depends on non-interruptible job scheduling and device-specific circuit optimization, so real-world gains may drop if orchestration or hardware availability is less favorable.
paper_title: Demonstration of Parallel Multi-QPU Execution for Fragment-Based Quantum Chemistry Using On-Premises Hardware
